chapter_theme: Two songs at Pakkam (பாக்கம்) on the body: food for crows, dogs and vultures at the pyre, carried by Death's trident, and the hut that wanders town to town in craving; the poet asks for the learning to string Murugan's names together and for the senses driven out so he can enter the house of release.

678.reading: The poet speaks of his body, dark as a cloud, with kin as many as the sea, food for crows, dogs, vultures and ghouls in the long fire of the burning ground, and of Death with his sharpened trident stabbing and carrying off the life, and asks Murugan to call him, grant him grace and give him the knowledge of texts to string his names into words. The praise names the vel that sent the demons fleeing to every quarter and freed the gods from prison, and Murugan, the jnana-master who spoke words full of devotion for those who wear the holy ash, at Pakkam where poets look on him with clusters of verse.
678.nuance: காக்கைக்கு நாய் கழுகு பேய்க்கு அக்கமான உடல்: the body is already apportioned to scavengers. The plea is for skill in verse (நாமமொழி கோக்கைக்கு நூலறிவு), again the gift of song. சாவருளி is unclear: it may be 'grant (escape from) death' or a different division. நீறுபுனைவார்க்கு ஒக்க ஞானபரனாய்ப் பத்தி கூர் மொழிகள் பகர் may point to Sambandar's hymns.

679.reading: The poet asks whether, rather than carrying this hut of a body that flocks of vultures will feed on, wandering from town to town, eyeing others' prosperity and standing in longing until he wilts, he will drive out the five senses, praise Murugan, and enter the house and rejoice. The praise names Vishnu, who bears the shining disc, sword, conch, mace and bow, whose hands the sea-waves wash, and who sleeps on the serpent bed in the milk sea, as uncle, at Pakkam where fish strike the areca and the cane.
679.nuance: வீட்டில் புகுந்திருந்து மகிழ்வேனோ: வீடு is both home and release, so the end of wandering from town to town is the house of liberation. ஆக்கத்தையும் தெரிந்து ஏக்கற்று: craving is aroused by seeing others' wealth.

links.note: Both set vultures on the body to answer its admirers: the Naladiyar shows them tearing at the stinking cart once its axle breaks, 679 calls the living body the hut they will feed on and makes it the reason to stop carrying it from town to town.

Tirumular asks what it matters if crows carry off the nest (காக்கை கவரிலென்) once the dancer who lived in the skin bag has left. The song calls the body, burning on the long pyre, already apportioned to crows, dogs, vultures and ghouls (காக்கைக்கு நாய் கழுகு பேய்க்கு அக்கமான உடல்). The same scavengers are named; Tirumular uses them to show the corpse no longer matters, the song to drive the plea for the gift of song before that end.

The Kural asks whether the life, lodging in the body as in a shelter (உடம்பினுள் துச்சில் இருந்த உயிர்க்கு), has found no home of its own (புக்கில்). The song pictures the body as a hut (குரம்பை) carried from town to town and asks to drive out the five senses and enter the house and rejoice (வீட்டிற் புகுந்திருந்து மகிழ்வேனோ), where வீடு is also release. The song names the home the Kural says the life has not yet found.

Tirumular says the six sects did not see the Lord; be clear, settle, and then enter the house without wavering (மாறுதல் இன்றி மனைபுகலாமே). The song asks to stop wandering from town to town and enter the house (வீட்டிற் புகுந்திருந்து). Both figure release as entering a house after restless movement, Tirumular's wandering being among sects and the poet's among towns and others' wealth.
